final_rationale: The verdict does not improve because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record into a narrower, caveated position. That narrowing matters: it correctly abandons any claim of clean certification and recognizes that aggregate readiness evidence cannot prove the named context passed. But under the stated policy, disclosure of material limitations or evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts is required unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. The present record still lacks admissible proof that the required disclosure has actually been inserted into the certification artifact or that an approved exception exists. So this is not a case where a caveated position is enough for compliant_with_caveats; the caveat itself is the unresolved compliance condition. The actor's reframing reduces overclaiming, but it does not convert the current record into demonstrated compliance.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the certification artifact or model card actually contains the required disclosure for the named deployment context.
No approved risk acceptance or equivalent governance approval is in evidence to substitute for the missing named-context evaluation coverage.
The actor's narrowed position is materially better than a clean-certification claim, but the caveat is still an unresolved compliance predicate rather than completed compliance on the present record.
Operational readiness evidence remains insufficient by itself to satisfy the model-card disclosure requirement for novelty-search note summarization.
